mission_note: Credential scheduling: rotation order, strategies, cooldowns, retry rounds, session affinity, auth_index surfaces. 'Batch api-key rotation' = rotation across a provider's api-key-entries pool (and cross-provider pools). Every multi-credential case MUST be able to show WHICH credential served WHICH request from the wire log, so the mock extensions below are required.

secrets_used_in_recordings.note: All synthetic, local-only. The upstream keys appear verbatim in fixtures (config fragment + wire log credential field) by design: they are the observable that distinguishes credentials.

baseline_config.deltas_note: Per-case deltas are listed per case (routing.strategy, request-retry, transient-error-cooldown-seconds, weights, session-affinity, extra provider). Apply via config edit + hot-reload is fine for phases WITHIN a case ONLY where the case says hot-reload is part of the test; otherwise restart the container between cases (rotation cursors reset on restart; cooldown state cleared on restart).

mock_extensions.needed_for: identifying which credential served which request (all multi-credential cases) and asymmetric per-credential / per-model failures (S4-04, S4-16)
requests: mock_openai.py / mocklib.py: append a "credential" field to each wire-log line = the Bearer api-key value from the Authorization header (keep Authorization itself redacted). Alternative: leave Authorization unredacted for S4 recordings only. Either way the fixture must show the serving key.

Control file may carry per-credential overrides: "by_key": {"<bearer api-key>": {"mode":"error","status":500}} — matched against the request Authorization Bearer value; falls back to the file top-level mode, then DEFAULTS. Used by S4-04.
Control file may carry per-upstream-model overrides: "by_model": {"<value of request body 'model'>": {"mode":"error","status":500}} — same precedence. Used by S4-16.
X-Mock-* per-request headers keep working; precedence X-Mock-* > by_key/by_model > top-level > defaults.
mock_extensions.fallback_if_declined: S4-04 alternative: two openai-compatibility providers each with one key, pointing at two mock_openai.py instances with independent control (needs a per-instance control path, e.g. control/<type>-<port>.json). S4-16 alternative: skip and keep the per-model isolation claim on S4-05/S4-06 model scoping only (weaker). The credential field has no alternative: without it rotation goldens cannot be verified — please include it.

fixture_format_notes: Per case: tests/fixtures/S4/<case-id>/ with meta.yaml, request.http, downstream.md, upstream.jsonl, mock-response.json exactly per BOOTSTRAP.md §7.

Multi-step cases: number requests/responses inside request.http / downstream.md (### 1, ### 2, ...) in execution order; upstream.jsonl keeps the full wire log for the case (mark the per-request split with comments or per-request files upstream-1.jsonl, upstream-2.jsonl if easier).

meta.yaml must list: config fragment used (exact YAML), control file contents at each step, mock mode at each step, sleeps applied, and the auth-ID -> api-key mapping for the recorded config (see determinism notes).
Wire-log 'ts' fields and inter-request gaps are dynamic; the ORDER and content of wire lines are the contract.
Mask ONLY listed dynamic_fields; cooldown durations appear as concrete numbers in fixtures (they are the contract under the pinned config).
determinism_notes: Credential order is defined by auth ID = '<kind>:<sha256[:12]>' where kind = 'openai-compatibility:mock-openai' and the hash covers NUL-joined [kind, api-key, base-url, proxy-url(''), ...]. Compute once per key to predict which key is 'first' (smallest ID): sha256(('openai-compatibility:mock-openai' + chr(0) + key + chr(0) + 'http://host.docker.internal:18999/v1' + chr(0)).encode()).hexdigest()[:12] — record the mapping in meta.yaml. The fixtures pin the observed order; CPA-Edge must reproduce the same order from the same config.
Fixed request body per step (given inline); identical bytes every replay. Cooldown waits use sleeps (given per step) so cooldown expiry is deterministic.
429 quota cooldown without Retry-After = 1 s (level 0 of the 1s*2^level ladder, cap 30 min); transient (500) with transient-error-cooldown-seconds: 2 = 2 s. Sleeps are sized with margin.

cases.purpose: Round-robin (default strategy) cycles the credential pool in ascending auth-ID order: first request is served by the smallest-ID credential; cursor advances only on pick; wrap-around after the largest ID.
cases.record: per request: status+headers+body (expect 200 + mock canned JSON each); upstream.jsonl: all 6 wire requests with serving credential
cases.expected: wire log credential sequence = [K_first, K_second, K_third, K_first, K_second, K_third] where K_* are the three keys in ascending auth-ID order (record mapping in meta.yaml). No cooldowns, no errors.
dynamic_fields: created field in canned response if dynamic
cases.determinism: Cursor + ID derivation fully deterministic for this config.

cases.purpose: fill-first pins every request to the first (smallest-ID) ready credential; no rotation while it stays healthy.
cases.record: status+headers+body x4 (200 each); upstream.jsonl with credential per request
cases.expected: all 4 wire requests carry the SAME credential = smallest-ID key; the other two keys are never hit.

cases.purpose: weighted-round-robin: smooth weighted selection converges to the configured ratio; zero-weight credentials are excluded while this strategy is active.
cases.config: baseline + routing.strategy: "weighted-round-robin" + weights: s4-oai-key-1 weight 3, s4-oai-key-2 weight 1, s4-oai-key-3 weight 0 (api-key-entries[].weight)
cases.record: status+headers+body x8 (200 each); upstream.jsonl with credential per request
cases.expected: 8 requests: the weight-3 credential is picked first and 6 times total, the weight-1 credential 2 times (smooth WRR; exact interleaving depends on ID order and is pinned by the fixture); the weight-0 credential NEVER appears. meta.yaml records the computed ID order.

cases.purpose: Same-request failover + transient cooldown + recovery under fill-first: (1) a 500 from the first credential fails over within the same request; (2) next requests skip the cooling credential; (3) after the 2 s transient cooldown the first credential is picked again (fill-first returns to head).

control.openai: {"by_key": {"<key with smallest auth-ID>": {"mode":"error","status":500}}} — compute the smallest-ID key first (see determinism_notes); record which key it is in meta.yaml

cases.record: per chat request: status+headers+body; full upstream.jsonl (with credential + status per hit)
cases.expected: R1 wire: [K1 -> 500, K2 -> 200], client gets 200 (failover hidden). R2/R3 wire: K2 only. R4 wire: K1 -> 200 (K1 recovered, fill-first returns to head).
cases.mock_upstream_mode: openai: happy + by_key error 500 on smallest-ID key

cases.purpose: When every credential is in a transient (non-quota) cooldown the next request returns HTTP 503 auth_unavailable with the enriched message (providers/model/last upstream error). Also proves the first request relays the last upstream error verbatim after failover exhaustion.
cases.record: per request: status+headers+body; upstream.jsonl
cases.expected: R1: wire hits both keys with 500 (failover within round 0); downstream = HTTP 500 with the mock error body VERBATIM (relay of the last upstream attempt). R2: NO upstream hit; downstream = HTTP 503, body {"error":{"message":"auth_unavailable: no auth available (providers=openai-compatibility-mock-openai, model=mock-model; last upstream error: rate_limit_exceeded: mock rate limit)","type":"server_error","code":"internal_server_error"}}.
cases.evidence_note: Raw-transcript precedent: probes/bootstrap-run1/mock-recordings/03-chat-stream-* recorded this exact 503 shape (BS §6 called it 500; the verbose transcript is authoritative).

cases.purpose: 429 quota cooldown: activation (1 s ladder level 0), the model_cooldown client shape while all credentials are quota-cooling, and automatic recovery after the window.
cases.record: per chat request: status+headers+body (include response headers: Retry-After on step 2); upstream.jsonl
cases.expected: R1: wire hits both keys (429 each); downstream = 429 with mock body VERBATIM. R2: no upstream hit; downstream = HTTP 429 + header Retry-After: 1 (or 0 if recorded late in the window) + body {"error":{"code":"model_cooldown","last_upstream_error":"rate_limit_exceeded: mock rate limit","message":"All credentials for model mock-model are cooling down via provider openai-compatibility-mock-openai (last error: rate_limit_exceeded: mock rate limit)","model":"mock-model","provider":"openai-compatibility-mock-openai","reset_seconds":<0|1>,"reset_time":"<0s|1s>"}} (keys alphabetically ordered). R3 (after 1.5s): served again — first wire hit is the next key in rotation order; downstream 200.
cases.evidence_note: Precedent: gemini m1 + wire notes recorded this shape with reset_time "1s"; transient-error-cooldown-seconds does NOT affect the 429 path.

cases.purpose: auth_index mapping + management-triggered cooldown recovery: GET management listing maps config credentials to auth-index values; POST /v0/management/reset-quota clears one credential's cooldown; error shapes for missing/unknown auth_index.

control.openai: steps 1-2: {"mode":"error","status":429}; before step 7: delete control file (happy)

requests.note: fresh container; both keys 429 -> quota cooldown (wire: K1 then K2)

body.auth_index: <auth-index of the SMALLEST-ID key (K1) from step 3>

after step 6 reset + DELETE the control file (back to happy)

Step 3: 200; provider entry lists api-key-entries[] each with deterministic 'auth-index' (16 lowercase hex chars) — record both values and the key mapping. cases.note: Steps 1-2 reproduce S4-06 state cheaply (can reuse the same container run as S4-06 if recorded back-to-back; then this fixture's steps 1-2 are the same requests).

cases.purpose: Caller-attributed 400 ends the request at the FIRST failing credential: no rotation, no second upstream hit, no cooldown.
cases.record: status+headers+body; upstream.jsonl
cases.expected: wire log has EXACTLY ONE upstream hit (the smallest-ID credential) with status 400; downstream = 400 with the mock error body VERBATIM.

cases.purpose: A provider-level request-scoped-errors rule with action "continue" reclassifies the matching 400 as credential-attributed: the request rotates to the next credential (no cooldown, no retry rounds).
cases.config: baseline + openai-compatibility entry gains request-scoped-errors: [{status: 400, match: ["mock rate limit"], action: "continue"}]
cases.record: status+headers+body; upstream.jsonl
cases.expected: wire log has TWO upstream hits (both keys, 400 each — rotation continued); downstream = 400 with the mock error body VERBATIM. Contrast with S4-08.

cases.purpose: request-retry: 1 starts an additional credential retry round after round 0 exhausted the pool: the gateway waits for the earliest cooldown (bounded by max-retry-interval), then re-admits every credential; the client sees one response.
cases.record: status+headers+body (single downstream response, ~2-2.5s after request start); upstream.jsonl (4 hits)
cases.expected: Round 0 hits all 3 keys in ascending auth-ID order (key-1, key-3, key-2), each 500; then a ~2.0-2.5s cooldown wait; round 1 repeats the same 3-key sweep (6 upstream hits total). Downstream = a single HTTP 500 response with the mock error body VERBATIM (relay of the last upstream attempt of round 1). No round 2 (request-retry is 1). Matches the recorded fixture (6 wire hits).
dynamic_fields: wire-log ts + inter-round gap duration (assert only: gap >= 2s)
cases.n3_fix_note: Round-1 review N3: earlier draft said '4 hits' from a 2-key mental model; baseline has 3 keys — corrected.

cases.purpose: routing.session-affinity: requests carrying an explicit session header stick to the credential bound for that session; requests without a session keep round-robin; different sessions bind independently.
cases.record: per request: status+headers+body; upstream.jsonl with credential per request
cases.expected: With keys sorted by auth ID as K1 < K2 < K3 (record mapping in meta.yaml): R1 -> K1 (RR fallback, no session). R2 (session A) -> K2 (new binding). R3 (session A) -> K2 (sticky cache hit). R4 (session B) -> K3 (new independent binding, RR successor). R5 (no session) -> K1 (RR fallback wraps). Wire sequence: K1, K2, K2, K3, K1.
cases.note: Requests without an explicit session header still form a derived session from the first-message hash fallback (identical bodies -> identical derived session -> same binding). R1 and R5 share the same body, so R5 is expected to hit the R1 binding (K1) — the recorded sequence is the contract either way.

cases.purpose: A mid-stream disconnect is a connection-lifecycle failure: the client keeps HTTP 200 with an in-stream error frame, and the credential is NOT cooled — the next request is served by the same credential (fill-first).
cases.record: step 1: FULL SSE byte stream (headers + every data: line + in-stream error frame); step 3: status+headers+body; upstream.jsonl
cases.expected: R1: HTTP 200, Content-Type text/event-stream; the mock's 2 events arrive as data: lines, then the connection hard-closes and the client receives an in-stream terminal frame data: {"error":{"message":"unexpected EOF","type":"server_error","code":"internal_server_error"}} (or the byte-exact recorded equivalent); no [DONE]. R3 (non-stream): served by the SAME credential as R1 (no cooldown from the lifecycle failure) — downstream 200.
cases.evidence_note: Precedent: gemini m3 recorded the same in-stream 'unexpected EOF' frame with HTTP 200 (probes/mocks).

cases.purpose: One alias mapped to several upstream model names rotates per request within the credential (intra-credential model pool), observable via the upstream request body's model field.
cases.config: baseline with api-key-entries reduced to ONLY s4-oai-key-1 (single credential — the pool offset is per credential, so extra keys would mask the rotation)
cases.record: status+headers+body x3; upstream.jsonl (request bodies!) — same credential throughout
cases.expected: All wire requests use the same single credential; the upstream body 'model' alternates by per-credential pool offset: R1 -> mock-pool-1, R2 -> mock-pool-2, R3 -> mock-pool-1. Client-side response 'model' field stays as recorded (no force-mapping).
cases.note: If recorded with all 3 keys instead, the pool rotation is confounded by credential rotation — keep 1 key for this case.

cases.purpose: All-credentials-401 yields the terminal authentication error (503 + authentication_error code) on the next request; the 30-minute unauthorized cooldown SURVIVES a config hot-reload.

requests.how: edit the mounted config.yaml (append a comment line '# s4 reload probe') and wait for the watcher reload log line

cases.record: per chat request: status+headers+body; docker log lines for the reload; upstream.jsonl
cases.expected: R1: wire hits both keys (401 each; API-key credentials cannot refresh); downstream = HTTP 401 with the mock error body VERBATIM. R2: NO upstream hit; downstream = HTTP 503, body {"error":{"message":"auth_unavailable: no auth available (providers=openai-compatibility-mock-openai, model=mock-model; last upstream error: rate_limit_exceeded: mock rate limit)","type":"authentication_error","code":"upstream_authentication_required","retryable":false}} (record byte-exact; the last-upstream-error suffix is expected because the 401 bodies parse as JSON). R3 (after config hot-reload): identical 503 terminal body — the 30-minute unauthorized cooldown survived the reload.

cases.purpose: Provider-level disable-cooling: transient 500s do NOT cool credentials — every request keeps failovering across the whole pool, no 503 ever appears.
cases.config: baseline + openai-compatibility entry gains disable-cooling: true
cases.record: per request: status+headers+body; upstream.jsonl
cases.expected: R1 AND R2: each hits BOTH keys (500 each, full failover both rounds); downstream = 500 with mock body VERBATIM both times. Never 503. Contrast with S4-05 (identical control, cooling on).

cases.purpose: A transient cooldown is scoped to the failed model: after both credentials cool on iso-model-1, a request for iso-model-2 is still served (per-model state isolation within each credential).
cases.record: per request: status+headers+body; upstream.jsonl
cases.expected: R1: wire hits both keys on upstream model mock-iso-1 (500 each); downstream 500 verbatim. R2: no upstream hit; 503 auth_unavailable (model=iso-model-1). R3 (iso-model-2): served 200 by the smallest-ID credential — the iso-model-1 cooldown did NOT block iso-model-2. R4: next credential in rotation (its iso-model-2 state is also clean) — 200.

cases.purpose: transient-error-cooldown-seconds: -1 disables ONLY transient cooldowns: 500s never cool (every request keeps failovering), while 429 quota cooldowns still activate and produce model_cooldown.
cases.record: per chat request: status+headers+body (incl. Retry-After on step 5); upstream.jsonl
cases.expected: R1 AND R2 (500 phase): each hits both keys; downstream 500 verbatim; never 503 (no transient cooldown). R4 (429 phase): hits both keys; downstream 429 verbatim. R5: no upstream hit; downstream 429 model_cooldown (quota cooldown ACTIVE despite -1) with Retry-After 1/0.
cases.evidence_note: Wire notes (parent relay): upstream 429 cooldown reset ~1s is NOT disabled by transient-error-cooldown-seconds: -1.

cases.purpose: Cross-provider pool: two provider families (gemini-api-key + openai-compatibility) exposing the same client model rotate across providers; a failing provider's requests fail over to the other provider.
cases.config: baseline + the EXACT YAML delta below — the second openai-compatibility provider MUST be a second list item under the top-level `openai-compatibility:` key (NOT under gemini-api-key). First recording attempt mis-nested it under gemini-api-key (fixture repurposed as S4-20); re-record with this YAML.
cases.control: phase A: both happy; phase B: {"gemini": {"mode":"error","status":500}}, openai happy
cases.record: per chat request: status+headers+body; BOTH wire logs (mock/logs/gemini.jsonl and mock/logs/openai.jsonl — copy both as upstream-gemini.jsonl / upstream-openai.jsonl)
cases.expected: Model 'mx' is served by two providers: gemini (gemini-api-key, 1 credential) and openai-compatibility-mock-openai-mx (1 credential). Provider list order = credential-count DESC then provider-name ASC -> [gemini, openai-compatibility-mock-openai-mx] (tie 1:1, 'gemini' < 'openai-...'). Phase A R1: mixed cursor at slot 0 -> gemini segment -> gemini credential serves 200 on the GEMINI wire (POST {gemini-base}/v1beta/models/gemini-mock-model:generateContent, x-goog-api-key auth). R2: cursor -> openai-mx segment -> openai-compat credential serves 200 on the OpenAI-compat wire (POST {openai-base}/chat/completions, Bearer s4-oai-key-1). Phase B (gemini mock error 500, transient 2s): R3 -> gemini 500 -> cooldown -> same-request failover -> openai-mx 200 (client sees 200). R4 -> gemini still cooling -> openai-mx 200. If the recording disagrees with the segment order, the fixture wins and the spec will be re-derived.

cases.purpose: Downstream-WebSocket requests prefer websocket-enabled codex credentials ACROSS priority tiers (shard path): a ws-enabled LOWER-priority credential is picked before a non-ws higher-priority one; when the ws attempt fails upstream, the request fails over to the next credential; a non-WS request on the same pool respects priority order (no preference).

requests.note: downstream-WS surface = Responses websocket transport: GET /v1/responses with Upgrade headers, then frames {"type":"response.create","model":"wsx","input":[...],"stream":...} (input MUST be an array; string input -> 400 'websocket request requires array field: input'; a frame without "type" -> 400 'unsupported websocket request type: '). /v1/ws is the wsrelay provider bridge, NOT this surface.
non-WS control request: priority order must win (cred-B first)

cases.record: step 1: full downstream WS byte stream (upgrade response + frames/close) + the codex mock wire log (the failed ws upgrade attempt carries cred-A's key; any failover HTTP request carries cred-B's); step 2: status+headers+body + wire log
cases.expected: Step 1 (downstream-WS via the Responses websocket transport: GET /v1/responses upgrade + {"type":"response.create","model":"wsx","input":[...],"stream":...} frames): cred-A (websockets:true, priority:-5) is attempted FIRST despite the lower priority tier — the codex mock receives GET /responses with Upgrade: websocket and Authorization: Bearer s4-codex-key-a (404; the mock cannot upgrade). The mock's 404 body carries a request-fault type tag ('invalid_request_error'), so rotation STOPS at cred-A (no failover) and the downstream WS client receives ONE error frame relaying the 404 verbatim: {"type":"error","status":404,"error":{"message":"<mock body>","type":"invalid_request_error"}}. Step 2 (plain HTTP chat): cred-B (priority 0) is picked first — single wire hit POST /responses 200. RECORDED DEVIATIONS vs the original derivation (fixture wins): (a) the downstream-WS surface is the Responses websocket transport (GET /v1/responses upgrade), NOT /v1/ws — /v1/ws is the wsrelay provider bridge; (b) no in-request failover after the ws attempt failed, because the 404 body is caller-attributed (request-fault stop, cf. S4-20). The WS-preference-pick observable (mandatory) is fully confirmed.

needs: websocket client (any minimal python ws client is fine)

cases.expected: R1 + R2 (count_tokens 404): EACH request sweeps BOTH gemini keys on the :countTokens path (rotation continued; NO cooldown set — that is why R2 hits the pool again instead of returning a scheduling error).
